result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give concrete, usable layouts: search moves to Home and its own tab, holds and checkouts merge into one tab, and both cover zero results, offline use and signed-out users. B pulls slightly ahead on search behavior. It gives grouped suggestions with a debounce, an ordered zero-results flow that retries automatically with fewer terms, other formats and branches, and searches the rest of the app. It also puts one-tap renew and the library card barcode on Home. A is stronger on what the app remembers, including preferred format, filters that stay set, and query and scroll position kept when going back. B covers less here. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put search on Home and in its own tab, and both give detailed typing and zero-result behavior. B goes further on what the app remembers: home branch, preferred format, filters that persist, and back navigation that keeps the query and scroll position. B also lays out the other main screens (My Items with renew and renew-all, Branches, Events) in more concrete terms. A has a slightly richer zero-results sequence and a nice one-tap renew on Home, but B is the more complete set of screens and behaviors.
